objective: Two defects in AUDIT/integrity-scan.mjs had made the series' chain-offender count wrong in the same direction, and #649 closed only the canonical-generation one. Units were selected by ^[A-Z]{1,4}-?\d{1,2}$, which demands an id ending in digits, so FIX-3B, FIX-3B2, FIX-3C, FIX-4A and FIX-4B were never scanned: their records were not hashed, field-checked, chain-walked or evidence-checked, and the broken link FIX-3B2/out -> FIX-3C@0ddf2771 was invisible outright. The script also never set an exit status, so it printed offenders and exited 0 -- any gate written against it passed with the chain broken. A unit is now any directory under the spec that holds a generation directory; SILENT-SKIP plus a failing exit fires if tracked generation records ever fall outside the scanned set; offences exit 1 with a RESULT line to gate on. Re-scanned with the scanner honest, the tree holds four offenders and seven canonical records no canonical parent named, not three and six. Each offender is closed by a new out-chain generation that changes only the forward pointer, leaving the record as first emitted in `out` untouched: E02 named E03 with a base E03 never had (E03's base is ba22f28a, FIX-5's result, and FIX-5/out already names E03), while the unit that branched from E02's result -- FIX-1 -- was named by nobody; FIX-2 named FIX-3, a conductor docs land of 131 files and 37 960 insertions that parseTaskManifest's 100-line ceiling makes impossible as a bootstrap unit, while FIX-3B, based on that docs land commit, was named by nobody; FIX-3C's record existed but sat outside every generation directory and named FIX-4, which the plan executed as FIX-4A and FIX-4B; T09's corrected record (R01, not the nonexistent T10) likewise sat outside every generation directory. Two records emitted terminal had successors: X07 -> X08 and V06 -> X01, the same situation X13/out-chain was created for.
